Leave the differential-expression table and a figure in results/.

119:- Outside the quorum-sensing genes the strongest changes were medium-specific. Phenazine biosynthesis genes fell hard in ΔrhlI (`phzG2` −5.4 in MMGluFeMinus; `phzC1`/`phzB1`/`phzF1` −6.3 to −6.7 in Succinate) and in the double mutant (`phzC2` −9.1, `phzB2` −8.8 in MMGluFePlus; `phzB1` −8.9 in Succinate). Denitrification genes `norB`/`norC`/`norD` fell −3.8 to −4.0 in ΔrhlI and −5.3 to −6.4 in ΔlasI in MMGluFeMinus. In MMGluFePlus both single mutants lost oxidative-stress genes (`katB` −8.2 and −5.9; `trxB2`, `ahpF`, `ahpC`), and in Succinate ΔlasI lost `lasI`, `chiC`, `pa1L` and `cpbD`. The double mutant added `rhlA` −8.1 in MMGluFeMinus and `lasA` −7.7 in Succinate. See [results/rnaseq_top_genes.csv](results/rnaseq_top_genes.csv).
123:- The largest single-mutant response was ΔlasI in Succinate (1,087 genes, 716 down), more than twice ΔrhlI in the same medium (416, 378 down); ΔrhlI in MMGluFePlus was also mostly down (346 of 533). ΔlasI's Succinate-specific set included `lasI` itself and the non-ribosomal peptide synthetase cluster `PA14_34810`/`PA14_34820`/`PA14_34830`/`PA14_34840`, while the double mutant's Succinate response was close to the union of the two singles (1,166 versus 1,188 genes). See [results/rnaseq_de_summary.csv](results/rnaseq_de_summary.csv).
132:- Chose FDR < 0.05 and |log2FC| ≥ 1 as the definition of a changed gene, reporting both the two-fold and FDR-only counts. See [results/rnaseq_de_summary.csv](results/rnaseq_de_summary.csv).
144:- [results/rnaseq_de_summary.csv](results/rnaseq_de_summary.csv) — one row per contrast: genes tested, changed at FDR < 0.05, changed at FDR < 0.05 and |log2FC| ≥ 1, up, down and outlier-flagged genes.

steps.text:
Done. I compared each mutant with wild type in each medium with DESeq2 (one saturated model over all 36 samples, then the nine within-medium contrasts), using FDR < 0.05 and |log2FC| ≥ 1 as the changed-gene definition.

**Genes changed (up/down), 2-fold and FDR-significant**

| Medium | ΔrhlI (97) | ΔlasI (98) | ΔlasIΔrhlI (99) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| MMGluFeMinus | 389 (209/180) | 384 (117/267) | 1,362 (684/678) |
| MMGluFePlus | 533 (187/346) | 461 (135/326) | 1,345 (549/796) |
| Succinate | 416 (38/378) | 1,087 (371/716) | 1,166 (386/780) |

Counting FDR alone gives 1,299–3,585 genes per contrast, so the two-fold set above is the conservative one.

**What stands out**

- The mutations themselves are visible: `lasI` is the strongest signal in the double mutant in every medium (−6.3 to −6.8; padj 8e-205 to 1e-230) and in ΔlasI in Succinate; `rhlI` drops in ΔrhlI (−1.6 to −2.3) and further in the double mutant; `rhlR` and `lasR` also fall in the double mutant.
- The strongest non-QS changes are medium-specific: phenazine biosynthesis genes in ΔrhlI and the double mutant, denitrification genes (`norB`/`norC`/`norD`) in both singles in MMGluFeMinus, oxidative-stress genes (`katB`, `ahpF`, `trxB2`) in both singles in MMGluFePlus, and `chiC`/`pa1L`/`cpbD` in ΔlasI in Succinate.
- The single mutants overlap far more than chance, but the shared fraction depends on medium: 78 shared genes in MMGluFeMinus, 214 in MMGluFePlus, 315 in Succinate (hypergeometric p 2e-20 to 1e-156). Direction agreement among shared genes is 79%, 98% and 99%; genome-wide log2FC correlations are 0.30, 0.53 and 0.66.
- In Succinate the response is very asymmetric: ΔlasI changes 1,087 genes versus 416 for ΔrhlI, with ΔlasI-specific changes including `lasI` and an NRPS cluster.
- The double mutant changes more genes than either single (793/674/213 genes changed in neither single) and behaves largely additively: its log2FC regressed on the sum of the two single-mutant log2FCs has slopes 1.04, 0.84 and 0.71 (R² 0.73–0.90). Double-specific examples include `lecB`, `rhlR`, `aprA` and `hsiB2`/`hsiF2`.

**Files**

- [analysis/rnaseq_differential_expression.R](analysis/rnaseq_differential_expression.R) — the reproducible analysis.
- [results/rnaseq_differential_expression.csv](results/rnaseq_differential_expression.csv) — full table, 52,452 rows (9 contrasts × 5,828 genes), with raw/shrunken log2FC, p-values, direction and Cook's-outlier flag.
- [results/rnaseq_de_summary.csv](results/rnaseq_de_summary.csv) — changed-gene counts per contrast.
- [results/rnaseq_mutant_overlap.csv](results/rnaseq_mutant_overlap.csv) — overlap, direction agreement, correlations and double-mutant additivity.
- [results/rnaseq_sensitivity.csv](results/rnaseq_sensitivity.csv) — per-medium refits and default Cook's-filter comparison.
- [results/rnaseq_top_genes.csv](results/rnaseq_top_genes.csv) — top ten genes per contrast by padj and by |log2FC|.
- [results/rnaseq_differential_expression.png](results/rnaseq_differential_expression.png) — changed-gene counts, single-mutant overlap, log2FC agreement, and a heatmap of the strongest genes.

The analysis and choices are also written up in [project-notes.md](project-notes.md#rna-seq-what-the-quorum-sensing-mutants-change-in-gene-expression). Five genes with a single Cook's-distance outlier (`rhlI`, `lasB`, `PA14_10540`, `PA14_30580`, `bkdB`) are flagged rather than removed; the sensitivity table shows the alternative counts change by at most five genes.

124:- The strain identities hold in the counts: `lasI` is near-absent in 98 and 99, and `rhlI` is strongly reduced in 97 (about 22% of wild type in MMGluFeMinus) and near-absent in 99. Five genes carry one Cook's-distance outlier each and are flagged rather than removed, among them `rhlI` and `lasB`. See [results/rnaseq_differential_expression.csv](results/rnaseq_differential_expression.csv).
134:- Chose to keep all genes and flag Cook's-distance outliers rather than let DESeq2 remove them. With three replicates the default filter removes five genes from every contrast entirely, including `rhlI` and `lasB`, because one replicate of each is an outlier; the counts change by at most five genes and the log2FC correlation is 1.000. See [results/rnaseq_sensitivity.csv](results/rnaseq_sensitivity.csv) and the `cooks_outlier` column of [results/rnaseq_differential_expression.csv](results/rnaseq_differential_expression.csv).

steps.text:
Created [results/summary.md](results/summary.md) — the project's three conclusions, each answered in two or three sentences with its key numbers and existing figure:

1. Single quorum-sensing mutants swarm worse than wild type; rhl mutants are more severe.
2. Mixing ΔrhlI and ΔlasI rescues swarming, peaking at 12.3:1.
3. The mutants change large, medium-specific gene sets; the single mutants overlap significantly and the double mutant is largely additive.

The file links the existing figures and result tables with document-relative paths, and [project-notes.md](project-notes.md) now points to it from the Files list. No new analysis was run.

# PA14 quorum sensing and swarming: conclusions

steps.text:
Created [results/summary.png](results/summary.png) — a 13 × 10 in, 300 dpi one-page figure with three labeled panels:

- **A — single mutants vs wild type:** geometric-mean colony area for wild type and the four mutants, with ratio vs wild type and 95% CI above each bar.
- **B — co-culture rescue:** colony area against the ΔrhlI:ΔlasI ratio (log scale), observed geometric means, the reported quadratic fit, the fitted peak at 12.3:1 (145,880; 1.34× wild type), and wild-type/single-mutant reference lines.
- **C — transcriptome changes:** up/down genes changed per mutant and medium (FDR < 0.05, |log2FC| ≥ 1).

The figure has a title, panel titles, axis labels, legends and a caption defining the thresholds, units and reference values, so it stands on its own. It was drawn only from the existing result tables; the co-culture curve is redrawn from the published quadratic estimates, with no refitting.

The plotting code is in [analysis/summary_figure.R](analysis/summary_figure.R), and [results/summary.md](results/summary.md) now links the one-page figure. [project-notes.md](project-notes.md) lists both under Files.
